what_changed: Federal Reserve proposes a Third-Party Risk Management Guide for Traditional Community Banking Organizations (under $30 billion in assets, not complex bank-fintech partnerships), a companion to the proposed all-bank TPRM guidance (2026-18859). Sec. IV.B covers operational resilience, system and information security, compliance with rules and regulations, and financial resilience of vendors; sec. IV.C gives vendor-by-vendor considerations for core, IT infrastructure, cybersecurity, payment processing and digital banking, loan management system, card, BSA/AML and fraud providers. The guide states it is not a rule, banks are not required to take the actions described, and consumer compliance is out of scope. Comments due November 16, 2026.
compliant_agent_must_now: No change until final. If adopted, Federal Reserve-supervised community bank clients would use the guide's operational resilience, information security, regulatory compliance and financial resilience considerations when onboarding and monitoring a servicing provider (likely treated like a loan management or payment-processing vendor).
open_questions_for_deploying_team: Which community bank clients are Federal Reserve-supervised state member banks under $30 billion, and which vendor category in sec. IV.C would they place the servicing agent in?
rationale: Full text confirms a proposed supervisory guide on how community banks examine vendors; within the test's vendor-examination clause. Confidence 0.85 rather than 0.9 because it is non-binding, Federal Reserve-only and excludes consumer compliance.
